IVY AND THE MOSSY LION: ivy gone up one whole flank in a lopsided sheet right to the square stone teeth along the top, the honey-coloured stone showing through in uneven flat-banded courses where the leaves thin out, and above the arch a fat carved stone lion's head jutting right out with real moss packed into its open mouth

THE SPOUT AND THE COPPER PANS: a stone spout high on the wall pouring a bright thread of rainwater down into a worn stone trough at the foot, wet dark streaks in flat pixel bands down the stone beneath every ledge, copper pans on iron hooks beside the little door, and two carved stone fish curled round a second spout above the arch with water coming out between their mouths

SNOW AND THE ORANGE SLITS: snow heaped a foot deep along every ledge and the walkway with icicles in a ragged fringe beneath, a warm orange glow coming out of every narrow slit window in flat amber bands, and a hanging bough of pine weighed down with snow and icicles strung right across the stone directly above the arch

FIREWOOD AND THE SLEEPING CAT: firewood stacked to a figure's shoulder in a long uneven heap against the wall, the stack stepping up in chunky pixel courses of ochre and dark brown, a striped cat asleep on the very top, and a fat carved stone owl's head the size of a barrel jutting straight out of the wall off to one side of the arch with pale lichen spread across its brow

THE PAPER LANTERNS: a row of round paper lanterns in saffron, coral and jade strung on a sagging rope along under the arch and three of them still unlit, the great blocks of warm amber stone below them in uneven flat-banded courses each face stepping into shadow through two flat dithered bands, and the rope itself looped over a carved stone fish head jutting out above the arch

THE TIMBER WHEEL AND THE ROPE: the enormous timber wheel and rope that lifts the heavy iron lattice gate mounted right out on the stone face to one side of the arch, its spokes worn pale at the grip, the portcullis bars half-raised and stopped, and above the arch a great counterweight of banded stone hanging in a timber frame on iron pins

THE ZIGZAG STAIR: a wooden stair zigzagging up the outside of the taller tower in three uneven flights, the treads stepping in hard pixel edges of warm timber against the grey-green stone, every landing a different size, and above the arch a wide shallow stone bowl brimming with water, two birds standing at its rim

THE HERB BUNDLES: long strings of drying herbs and onions hanging from iron hooks down one whole side of the wall in ragged overlapping layers of dusty green and amber, the stone behind them in honey-coloured flat-banded courses with every joint dark, and above the arch a bundle of dried flowers as wide as a figure tied with a bright red cord

THE DOVECOTE TOWER: a dovecote built onto the side of the shorter and fatter of the two towers, its little round holes stepping up in an uneven grid with birds going in and out, the stone of the main wall in warm biscuit-coloured flat-stepped bands below it, and directly above the arch a timber hoist arm with a rope and hook swinging gently out over the road

THE BRAZIER IN THE NICHE: a brazier burning low in a deep niche cut into the wall to the right of the arch, a blackened kettle sitting beside it on a flat stone, the niche walls dark with old smoke stepping back in three flat dithered bands, and above the arch a great bronze bell hung on a stout timber yoke, its surface gone green at the shoulder

THE CROOKED TREE: a whole crooked tree grown out of a crack high up on the wall's face, its roots spread flat across the stone in a dark splayed fan, small yellow leaves against the amber stone, and above the arch a nest of sticks as wide as two arms built into the ledge with a long-legged bird standing in it and one chick visible

THE BEEHIVE IN THE NICHE: a straw beehive tucked into a broad niche in the wall at shoulder height, a slow drift of bees in the air around it, the honey-coloured stone on either side in uneven flat-banded courses each face stepping two flat dithered shades into shadow, and off to one side of the arch a carved stone bear's head as broad as a cart wheel jutting straight out of the wall, its muzzle worn pale and smooth

THE ROPE-AND-BASKET HOIST: a rope-and-basket hoist running from a high window down to the ground below, the basket mid-air with a net of round gourds in it, the stone face it runs against in warm amber courses stepping in hard pixel blocks, and above the arch three long strips of bright cloth in scarlet, saffron and jade twisting edge-on in the wind, hung from a pole bolted to the stone

THE SMALL SHRINE: a small shrine set into the stone to one side of the arch, a shallow bowl of orange flowers on its ledge with one tallow candle burning at the left and two dark on the right, the surrounding stone in biscuit-coloured flat-banded courses with the joints showing dark, and above the arch a carved wooden beam-end shaped like a curling fish jutting out a full arm's length

THE WET WALL AFTER RAIN: every surface of the stone dark and wet after rain, the colours gone deep amber and charcoal in flat dithered bands stepping across each block face, a bright puddle at the foot of the wall under every ledge, and above the arch a fat stone lion's head jutting right out with a thin bright thread of water running from the corner of its open mouth

WINDOW BOXES AT UNEVEN HEIGHTS: window boxes crammed with red and yellow flowers at five uneven heights on the wall face, each box a different width, the soil dark against the pale honey stone below in flat-banded courses of warm amber stepping into shadow through two flat dithered bands, and above the arch one wide window box spilling trailing green stems down over the stone

THE SMALL DOOR IN THE BIG DOOR: a small low door cut into one of the two great timber doors standing wide open flat against the wall, warm yellow light spilling out of the small one across the stone threshold in a long stepped pixel trapezoid, the door's own planks in chunky flat banded rows of dark amber, and off to one side of the arch a carved stone owl's head the size of a barrel jutting straight out of the wall with lichen in pale patches across its brow

NETS AND BASKETS ON IRON HOOKS: nets, baskets and copper pans on iron hooks covering the wall between the arch and the left tower in an uneven overlapping cluster, three hooks high and the lowest one bent out of line, the stone behind in flat warm amber courses each face stepping into shadow through two dithered bands, and above the arch a shallow stone basin of water with a pair of birds splashing in it

THE LONG DRIFT AND THE SHOVELLED PATH: a long drift of snow banked up against the wall's foot with a shovelled path cut through it, the cut face of the snow showing in flat white and blue-shadow pixel bands, the stone above it in honey-coloured uneven courses every edge a hard pixel step, and above the arch a row of icicles hanging from a thick ledge of snow heaped a foot deep on the stone

MOSS AND FERNS ON THE SHADED SIDE: the entire shaded side of the wall covered in moss and small ferns in every joint, the stone beneath in dark greenish-amber flat-banded courses stepping back two dithered shades on every face, the ferns at three uneven heights each a slightly different green, and above the arch a carved stone face with a beard of thick moss and one fat fern growing from the right eyebrow

THE ROLLED MATS AND THE LADDER: rolled mats leaning against the wall at two different angles and a ladder resting where it was left against the stone beside them, its rungs in hard pixel steps of pale timber, the wall behind in warm uneven flat-banded amber stone courses, and above the arch a stone ledge with snow heaped a foot deep along it and a row of icicles hanging unevenly beneath

IRON LAMPS AT UNEVEN HEIGHTS: iron lamps on brackets at five uneven heights down the right side of the wall, three of them lit and casting overlapping circles of amber across the stone face and two still dark, the stone itself in honey-coloured flat-banded courses each face stepping into shadow through three flat dithered bands, and above the arch the tallest bracket holding a large round lantern in warm orange

THE COUNTERWEIGHT FRAME: a great counterweight of banded stone hanging in a heavy timber frame bolted to the wall beside the arch, the stone banded in stripes of charcoal and pale grey in flat pixel courses, the timber frame in chunky dark brown stepped blocks, and directly above the arch the portcullis rope running up through a wide iron ring fixed to the stone, the iron lattice gate half-raised and stopped

THE NARROW SLIT WINDOWS WITH BIRDS: birds' nests crammed into every narrow slit window up the full height of the taller tower, straw and twigs poking out of each one at different lengths, the tower face in warm amber stone courses stepping in hard pixel edges, three long strips of bright cloth in coral, gold and deep green twisting edge-on from poles at the top, and above the arch a wide nest with a speckled egg just visible over the rim

THE WET STREAKS AND THE TROUGH: wet dark streaks running down the stone face in flat pixel bands beneath every ledge, a bright copper-coloured puddle at the foot of the wall catching the light, the stone itself in uneven honey-coloured courses each block face stepping into shadow through two flat dithered bands every edge a hard pixel step, and above the arch a stone spout pouring a bright thin thread of water down in a clean arc into a worn stone trough below
